resources.string: agentreins-moblie uses apps for you on a separate virtual screen, so you can keep using your phone. For this it borrows Android’s built-in “USB debugging” and “Wireless debugging”: pair once and agentreins-moblie connects automatically from then on — no computer needed. Web and file tasks work without this.
You can skip this for now and just use web, files and chat; agentreins-moblie will remind you the first time it needs an app.
Open “About phone” in Settings and tap “Build number” 7 times until you see “You are now a developer”. On some phones “Build number” is under “Software information”.
In “Developer options”, find “USB debugging”, turn it on and tap “OK” when asked. No cable needed: with it on, agentreins-moblie can keep working even when Wi-Fi is off.

Find agentreins-moblie in your system’s “Accessibility” settings and turn it on. Then agentreins-moblie reads the pairing code by itself when pairing — no typing needed. You can also skip this (recommended): after pairing, agentreins-moblie turns it on by itself without being blocked by Android’s “restricted setting”, and this time you enter the code from the notification.
agentreins-moblie reads the pairing code itself

In “Developer options”, find “Wireless debugging” and turn it on. When asked, choose “Allow” and tick “Always allow on this network” so you won’t be asked again. You need to be on Wi-Fi (internet access not required).
Just be on Wi-Fi; no internet needed
Open “Wireless debugging”, then tap “Pair device with pairing code”. A 6-digit code appears on screen.
Once paired, agentreins-moblie connects and gets ready by itself in a few seconds.
Skip (agentreins-moblie turns it on after pairing)
Can’t turn it on? Allow restricted settings in App info first
When the code appears, wait a few seconds — agentreins-moblie reads it and finishes pairing. No need to leave that page.
Tap any step above to go back and redo it.
agentreins-moblie reads “Developer options” as off (some phones report it wrong). Go back and make sure it’s on.
“Wireless debugging” seems to be off: agentreins-moblie reads it as off. Go back and make sure it’s on and you’re on Wi-Fi.
This phone doesn’t let agentreins-moblie read the “Wireless debugging” switch. Go back and make sure it’s on and you’re on Wi-Fi.
Found the pairing window. Enter the code in the notification.
The pairing code goes into a notification, so allow agentreins-moblie’s notifications first.
“Needs you” and “Task results” notifications won’t pop up now, so you may miss when you’re needed. You can continue, or turn them on now.
The pairing window closes when you leave it. Use split screen to see the code and type here at the same time.
The number after the colon in “IP address & port” in the pairing window
Only needed if agentreins-moblie can’t find the pairing window
Pairing and connecting, just a few seconds
Keep USB debugging on. After a restart, turn on Wireless debugging and agentreins-moblie reconnects automatically.
The code changes each time the pairing window opens. Tap “Pair device with pairing code” again and enter the new 6 digits.
Keep the window showing the code open while you enter it. Open it again and retry.
agentreins-moblie needs Wi-Fi to start phone control (no internet needed). It resumes by itself once you join any Wi-Fi.
Wireless debugging isn’t allowed on this Wi-Fi yet

agentreins-moblie turned on Wireless debugging, but the system didn’t allow it on this Wi-Fi. Turn on “Wireless debugging” once yourself; when asked, tick “Always allow on this network” and tap Allow. After that agentreins-moblie can turn it on by itself on this Wi-Fi.
Couldn’t find the Wireless debugging port. You can: turn “Wireless debugging” off and on again, then retry; switch to a phone hotspot or your home Wi-Fi; or enter the port below.
The system may have revoked it after a long time unused, or it was removed. Just pair again. Turn on “Disable adb authorization timeout” in Developer options so it won’t expire again.
Retry first; if that doesn’t work, pair again.
Uses wireless debugging to control apps on a virtual screen

After pairing once, agentreins-moblie’s built-in helper stays in the background and keeps working even without Wi-Fi. Keep “USB debugging” (in Developer options) on; turning it off stops phone control. After a restart, join Wi-Fi and turn on “Wireless debugging” and agentreins-moblie reconnects by itself — no new code needed.
Connected and able to use apps
Connected; stops if Wi-Fi drops unless “USB debugging” is on
Not paired yet; set it up once before using apps
Paired; connects automatically once Wireless debugging is on
No Wi-Fi; resumes once you join any Wi-Fi
Turn on Wireless debugging once yourself and tick “Always allow on this network”
If it won’t connect, or after changing phone settings
Delete the pairing and stop phone control

agentreins-moblie will delete the pairing, stop using apps on the virtual screen, and revoke the permissions granted through the switches below. Web and file tasks aren’t affected. To use apps again later, you’ll need to pair once more. You can also remove agentreins-moblie under “Wireless debugging → Paired devices” in system settings.
Phone control isn’t ready, so agentreins-moblie can’t use apps this time; web and files work as usual.
Type the 6 digits shown on screen here — no need to leave the pairing window
Phone control is set up. You can go back to agentreins-moblie now
Go back to agentreins-moblie to see how to fix it
Wrong or expired code: in the pairing window, tap “Pair device with pairing code” again to get a new code, then enter it again
The pairing window closed or the code expired: tap “Pair device with pairing code” again to get a new code, then enter it again
agentreins-moblie’s notification pops up at the top of the screen; if not, swipe down to open the notification shade
The pairing code goes into a notification, so turn on agentreins-moblie’s “%1$s” notifications first.

agentreins-moblie’s “%1$s” notifications won’t pop up at the top of the screen now. Turn on “Pop on screen” so you can enter the code right over the pairing window; otherwise swipe down to the notification shade to enter it.
Looking for the Wireless debugging port on this phone…
On the “Wireless debugging” page, the number after the colon in “IP address & port”, e.g. 41235
